title: Persist the declared actor/accountable-human on task records; no audit trail today
description: Raised by opum-cli-e2e (2026-09-07) while building LCLI-434's provenance-verification rows: quest 0.4.0 requires an explicit --actor/--actor-kind[/--accountable-human] declaration on every write (enforced at the boundary, denied with exit 4 without one), but the declared actor is never persisted on the resulting task record and there is no audit/history command to recover it after the fact. Confirmed by direct on-disk inspection and source read, not taken on a peer's word: TaskState (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts) has no actorId/actorKind/accountableHumanId field alongside its other tracked fields (createdAt/updatedAt are the closest analogues and both exist), and grepping src/cli/main.ts for a history/audit command surface returns nothing. So a write's declared actor is checked once and then lost -- LCLI-434's rows cannot verify who made a change after the fact, only that someone declared themselves at write time. Recording actor/accountable-human on the record (or in an append-only event log) is what would let provenance be verified later; every write already carries the declaration this would consume, so the input exists today, only the persistence and read path are missing. One relevant lead, not a prescribed design: src/domain/records.ts already defines an unused TaskEvent/appendTaskEvent/materializeTask event-sourcing primitive (schemaVersion, eventId, operationId, taskId, actorId, basis, patch) with its own append-only-and-operation-idempotent semantics and replay-consistency check (assertReplayMatches) -- confirmed via grep that nothing in src/application/ or src/cli/ imports or calls any of the three, so this is scaffolding that predates the current plain-record write path and was never wired in, not a currently-dead-but-load-bearing mechanism. Whether persisting attribution reuses this event log, adds a simpler actor/accountableHuman field pair directly to TaskState, or takes some other shape is an open design question for whoever picks this up, not settled by this filing. Deferred by orchestrator ruling (opum-agent, 2026-09-07): not scheduled for the fleet backlog campaign's wave 3 (0.5.0) release unless quest-cli itself judges it a bug rather than a feature gap -- judged here as a feature gap (the manifest and current contract never promised persisted attribution, only enforced declaration at write time), so it stays deferred. The orchestrator sequences it after the campaign.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A task record (or an accompanying append-only log) retains who made each write and, for a delegated agent, who they were accountable to, recoverable after the fact rather than only enforced at write time
A command surface (existing or new) can answer 'who changed this and when' for at least the most recent write to a given task, without requiring git history
The chosen shape (persisted field vs. event log vs. something else) is a deliberate design decision recorded in the task, not an incidental side effect of an unrelated change
Existing regression tests for actor declaration/enforcement keep passing; new tests cover the persistence and retrieval path
